details: The scoped package @zmtcdn/components publishes a sentinel version (9999.0.0) containing only package.json, a 21-byte index.js stub and postinstall.js; package.json declares "postinstall": "node postinstall.js", so the script runs on every install. It builds a JSON payload from the build host — hostname, OS platform, local username, current working directory, ISO timestamp and Object.keys(process.env), i.e. the NAMES of every environment variable, which in CI environments include NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, SLACK_TOKEN, DOCKER_PASSWORD, CI_JOB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN and HF_TOKEN — and POSTs it over HTTPS to hxxps://webhook[.]site/f52af355-4783-4acb-9de1-5e44b5963025. The script sends variable names and their presence, not their values, and reads no files. The same postinstall script with the destination hxxps://www[.]hinny[.]shop/api is shipped in the sibling package @zmtcdn/ui@9999.0.7. This package is a dependency-confusion implant: a scoped name published at the sentinel version 9999.0.0 in an 852-byte tarball (3 files) whose only code is the lifecycle hook package/postinstall.js, declared as `"postinstall": "node postinstall.js"`. Installing the package therefore executes the hook, which builds a JSON fingerprint of the build host — os.hostname(), os.platform(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), an ISO timestamp, and Object.keys(process.env), i.e. the complete list of environment variable NAMES present in the install environment (including CI/CD and registry credential variable names such as NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITLAB_TOKEN, DOCKER_PASSWORD, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) — and POSTs it over HTTPS to hxxps://webhook[.]site/f52af355-4783-4acb-9de1-5e44b5963025 (POST, path /f52af355-4783-4acb-9de1-5e44b5963025, port 443, Content-Type application/json, ~1788-byte body). The purpose of the beacon is to confirm that an internal/scoped package name resolves to an externally controlled publish and to inventory which credential-bearing variables the victim's build environment exposes, so the same channel can be followed by targeted theft. The hook is a self-contained 646-byte script with no obfuscation, no second-stage download, no eval/Function use and no file reads; its only outbound destination is the webhook[.]site callback above. Indicator: hxxps://webhook[.]site/f52af355-4783-4acb-9de1-5e44b5963025.
